title_en: All-in-One Dashboard for Email Marketing
source_md:
Email Marketing

 All-in-One Dashboard for Email Marketing

Monitor Campaign, Workflow, and Bulk Action email performance from one unified Email Statistics dashboard in HighLevel.

What You'll Learn

HighLevel's All-in-One Dashboard for Email Marketing brings performance data from **Campaigns**, **Workflows**, and **Bulk Actions** into one Email Statistics experience. You can compare engagement, filter reporting by email source, review top-performing emails, and export statistics without collecting data from multiple areas.

The dashboard also makes it easier to move from a high-level engagement summary into detailed performance trends. This article explains how to access the dashboard, interpret its reporting areas, use filters and sample data, understand Workflow reporting, export statistics, and troubleshoot common reporting questions.

Email Statistics Dashboard vs. Email Widgets

The All-in-One Email Marketing Dashboard is the **Email Statistics** experience under **Marketing → Emails → Statistics**. It is separate from configurable Email Widgets that can be added to a sub-account Dashboard or Custom Report.

# **What is the All-in-One Dashboard for Email Marketing?**

The All-in-One Dashboard for Email Marketing is a centralized reporting experience in HighLevel that brings together email statistics from Campaigns, Workflows, and Bulk Actions. Instead of checking each sending method separately, you can use one Email Statistics dashboard to review overall performance and compare engagement across supported email sources.

The dashboard is available under **Marketing → Emails → Statistics** and provides Engagement Summary reporting, Performance Analysis, email-source filtering, Top Performing Emails, date controls, and related reporting tools.

## **Key Benefits of the All-in-One Dashboard**

A unified reporting view makes it easier to compare email performance and identify trends without switching between separate Campaign, Workflow, and Bulk Action reporting areas. This reduces reporting friction while helping teams identify stronger-performing email activity more quickly.

- **Unified Email Reporting:** Review Campaign, Workflow, and Bulk Action email statistics from one location.
- **Source-Level Filtering:** Narrow the dashboard to a specific email source when you need a more focused view.
- **Performance Visibility:** Monitor delivery and engagement trends through summary and performance reporting.
- **Top-Performer Insights:** Identify emails generating stronger open or click engagement.
- **Workflow Granularity:** Review individual Workflow email actions rather than treating an entire Workflow as one email.
- **Sample Reporting:** Preview the reporting experience with sample data when the option is available.
- **CSV Exporting:** Export Email Statistics data for external analysis, reporting, or sharing.

## **What Data is Included in the Dashboard?**

Email Statistics consolidates supported email-sending sources into one reporting experience. Understanding how each source is represented is especially important when comparing automated Workflow emails with one-time Campaign or Bulk Action sends.

| Dashboard Filter | What It Represents |
| --- | --- |
| **All Campaigns** | Combined reporting across the supported email sources in Email Statistics. |
| **Email Campaigns** | Email marketing Campaign sends. |
| **Workflow Campaigns** | Emails sent through Workflow email actions. |
| **Bulk Action Campaigns** | Emails sent through Contacts → Bulk Actions. |

The All-in-One Dashboard focuses on email activity. SMS and other messaging-channel statistics are not part of this Email Statistics view.

## **Understanding Dashboard Metrics and Performance Areas**

The dashboard organizes reporting into summary and performance areas so you can move from an overall view of email activity into more detailed engagement trends. Reviewing these areas together helps distinguish high-level delivery performance from changes in recipient engagement over time.

### **Engagement Summary**

Engagement Summary provides a combined visual view of how recipients interact with emails across the selected reporting scope. When multiple sources are included, the chart can show how Email Campaigns, Workflow Campaigns, and Bulk Action Campaigns contribute to the overall results.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080535170/original/2vU78YnhZ4MK_XcRSTZUwY_mCAomaPpH-Q.png?1788980889)

### **Performance Analysis**

Performance Analysis helps you evaluate email trends over time using delivery and engagement metrics. The available controls let you review metrics across the selected reporting period and compare performance across the email sources included in the current view.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080535211/original/kj19Psipu3y7NXb91vgk5gMxNOh41O1xfA.png?1788980983)

**Data timing:** Most email statistics update in near real time. Some engagement events can take a few minutes to appear depending on recipient activity and provider delays.

For definitions of individual email metrics, see [Email Statistics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001215386).

## **Filtering Email Statistics by Source**

Source filtering helps isolate the email activity you want to evaluate. This is useful when combined reporting is too broad and you need to analyze Email Campaigns, Workflow Campaigns, or Bulk Action Campaigns independently.

1. Go to **Marketing → Emails → Statistics**.
2. Open the source dropdown near the top-left of the dashboard.
3. Select **All Campaigns** to review the combined view.
4. Select **Email Campaigns**, **Workflow Campaigns**, or **Bulk Action Campaigns** to narrow the dashboard to that source.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080535335/original/BRXSn_xipM-iblt7yjEJ0Dviq-oWJwcCvg.png?1788981181)

## **Using Sample Data**

Sample data can help you preview the Email Statistics reporting experience before you have enough live email activity to populate the dashboard. When the option is available, it provides demonstration values for understanding the dashboard layout without treating those values as actual performance.

If **Try Sample Data** appears in your dashboard, click it to preview the reporting experience.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080535390/original/2RBKOeJLRPYUGdqdv-xIAEfoIHjAKmbRtg.png?1788981276)

### **Identify When Sample Data is Active**

When sample statistics are active, the dashboard displays a notice identifying the values as sample data. Use **Clear Sample Data** when you want to remove the demonstration values.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080535410/original/N6z6KtPPrDU8YQo3K7f8mVoazKEAxS03Xw.png?1788981315)

**Screenshot:** Email Statistics while sample data is active, including the sample-data notice and Clear Sample Data control.

**Important:** Sample statistics are demonstration data and should not be interpreted as actual Campaign, Workflow, or Bulk Action performance.

## **Understanding Top Performing Emails**

Top Performing Emails helps identify email content generating stronger engagement. Results can be evaluated using available engagement metrics such as open or click rates, but the way an item is represented depends on whether the email came from a Campaign, Bulk Action, or Workflow.

Important Workflow Reporting Detail

For **Workflows**, Top Performing Emails reports the performance of **individual email actions**, not the entire Workflow sequence as one email.

| Source | Top Performing Emails Represents |
| --- | --- |
| **Email Campaigns** | The individual Campaign email send. |
| **Bulk Action Campaigns** | The individual Bulk Action email send. |
| **Workflow Campaigns** | Each individual email action inside the Workflow. |

## **How to Set Up the All-in-One Dashboard for Email Marketing**

No separate feature configuration is required once Email Statistics is available in your sub-account. Proper use comes down to opening the correct reporting area, selecting the appropriate source and date range, and interpreting the summary and performance areas in the context of how the email was sent.

1. Go to **Marketing → Emails → Statistics**.
2. Use **All Campaigns** when you want a combined view across supported email sources.
3. Use the source dropdown to focus on **Email Campaigns**, **Workflow Campaigns**, or **Bulk Action Campaigns** when needed.
4. Select the date range that matches the email activity you want to analyze.
5. Review **Engagement Summary** for a high-level view.
6. Scroll to **Performance Analysis** to review trends and available performance metrics.
7. Continue to **Top Performing Emails** to identify stronger-performing individual sends or Workflow email actions.

**Bulk Action shortcut:** If you begin under Contacts → Bulk Actions, open the applicable send's statistics and use **Load More Stats** to access the broader Email Statistics dashboard.

## **Exporting Email Statistics**

CSV export makes it possible to analyze Email Statistics outside HighLevel or share performance data with stakeholders. You can export combined email activity or focus on specific sources such as Email Marketing Campaigns, Workflows, or Bulk Actions.

1. Go to **Marketing → Emails → Statistics**.
2. Choose the reporting type you want to export.
3. Click **Export**.
4. Enter the email address or addresses that should receive the export.
5. Open the email containing the download link and download the CSV file.

| Export Type | Reporting Scope |
| --- | --- |
| **All Campaigns** | All supported email activity visible in Email Statistics, including Campaigns, Workflows, and Bulk Actions. |
| **Email Marketing Campaigns Only** | Email Campaign performance from Marketing → Emails → Campaigns. |
| **Workflows Only** | Individual Workflow email-action performance. |
| **Bulk Actions Only** | Emails sent through Contacts → Bulk Actions. |

Export download links are delivered by email and remain available for a limited period. Recent export records can also be reviewed from the Email Campaigns settings area.

For complete instructions and export-retention details, see [Exporting Email Marketing Data](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007499-exporting-email-marketing-data).

## **Troubleshooting Email Marketing Dashboard Reporting**

When dashboard data does not look as expected, verify how the email was sent, which source and date range are selected, and whether the event may still be processing. The configured sending provider can also affect which delivery and engagement events are available in reporting.

| Issue | What to Check |
| --- | --- |
| **Expected email activity is missing** | Verify how the email was sent and confirm the correct source and date range are selected. |
| **A Workflow appears as several emails** | This is expected in Top Performing Emails because Workflow email actions are tracked individually. |
| **Recent engagement is not visible yet** | Allow a few minutes for applicable engagement events to appear. |
| **A Bulk Action email is difficult to find** | Look under Bulk Action Campaigns in the source filter, or open the Bulk Action's statistics and use Load More Stats. |
| **Some statistics are missing** | Check the configured email provider and review the dedicated troubleshooting guidance because the events available to HighLevel can vary by provider. |
| **The dashboard shows demonstration values** | Check for a sample-data notice and clear the sample data before interpreting the dashboard as live email performance. |

For deeper diagnostic steps, see [Troubleshooting Email Statistics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001208601).

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

Q: Where is the All-in-One Email Marketing Dashboard?

Go to **Marketing → Emails → Statistics**. This opens the unified Email Statistics dashboard.

Q: What email sources are included?

The dashboard combines email statistics from Email Campaigns, Workflow Campaigns, and Bulk Action Campaigns.

Q: Why are Workflow emails listed separately in Top Performing Emails?

Workflow reporting tracks the individual email actions inside a Workflow. Top Performing Emails therefore evaluates those actions separately instead of treating the full Workflow sequence as one email.

Q: Can I export data from Email Statistics?

Yes. Email Statistics supports CSV exports for combined email activity and specific sources such as Email Marketing Campaigns, Workflows, and Bulk Actions.

Q: How quickly do email statistics update?

Most email statistics update in near real time. Some events can take a few minutes to appear depending on recipient activity and provider delays.

Q: Why am I seeing sample data?

If sample data is active, the dashboard displays demonstration values so you can preview the reporting experience. Use **Clear Sample Data** when you want to remove those values.

Q: Is this the same as adding Email Widgets to a Dashboard?

No. Email Statistics is the unified reporting experience under Marketing → Emails. Email Widgets are separate configurable reporting components that can be added to sub-account Dashboards and Custom Reports.

### **Related Articles**

[Email Statistics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001215386) [Exporting Email Marketing Data](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007499-exporting-email-marketing-data) [Troubleshooting Email Statistics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001208601) [Email Statistics – Summary Page](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006834) [Email Widgets for Dashboards and Reporting](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004328-email-widgets) [Getting Started - Launch an Email Campaign](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005059-getting-started-launch-an-email-campaign)

title_en: Electrician’s Guide to Maximizing Your Business with HighLevel
source_md:
As an electrician, you’re already skilled at wiring homes, troubleshooting issues, and keeping your customers safe. But in today’s market, success also depends on being found online, engaging with leads immediately, and showcasing your reputation. In this guide, you’ll learn five key strategies to help you:

- Generate more high-quality leads.
- Automate follow-ups so no opportunity slips through.
- Build a powerful reputation with automated review collection.
- Run small, high-impact ad campaigns.
- Maintain visibility through regular social media updates.

Whether you’re new to these features or looking to deepen your current setup, this guide will help you optimize HighLevel to support your growth.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [1. Get Found on Google & Dominate Local Search](#1.-Get-Found-on-Google-&-Dominate-Local-Search)
- [2. Automate Follow-Ups & Capture Every Lead](#2.-Automate-Follow-Ups-&-Capture-Every-Lead)
- [3. Automate Reviews & Build a Stellar Reputation](#3.-Automate-Reviews-&-Build-a-Stellar-Reputation)
- [4. Launch a Small, High-ROI Ad Campaign](#4.-Launch-a-Small,-High-ROI-Ad-Campaign)
- [5. Stay Visible with Consistent Social Media Updates](#5.-Stay-Visible-with-Consistent-Social-Media-Updates)
- [6. Your Next Steps](#6.-Your-Next-Steps)
- [7. Need to Upgrade Your HighLevel Account?](#7.-Need-to-Upgrade-Your-HighLevel-Account?)
- [8. Proven Strategies for Electricians using HighLevel](#8.-Proven-Strategies-for-Electricians-using-HighLevel)

---

## **1. Get Found on Google & Dominate Local Search**

#### **Why This Matters**

Being visible on Google is essential—most customers rely on online searches to find local services. Optimizing your online presence ensures that you are the first choice when potential clients need an electrician.

- **Visibility Counts:** Most customers hire the first electrician they find on Google.
- **Double Your Leads:** Optimizing your Google presence can significantly increase the number of customers reaching out to you.

#### **What You Need to Do**

Claim and verify your Google Business Profile, define your service areas, and integrate call tracking and automated review strategies to boost your local search ranking.

- **Claim & Verify Your Google Business Profile (GMB):**If you haven’t done this, you may be invisible to potential customers. Follow our [Google Business Profile setup guide](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177?hl=en) to get started.
- **Set Up Service Areas:**List all the cities and neighborhoods you serve to appear in local search results.
- **Call Tracking:** Replace your listing number with a HighLevel tracking number to pinpoint which efforts are driving calls. [Learn more about setting up call tracking](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001179764-call-tracking-and-missed-call-text-back-through-google-business-profile).
- **Automate Google Reviews:** Use HighLevel to send review requests automatically after each job—more 5-star reviews mean better rankings. [See our guide on automating reviews](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003873-how-to-setup-workflow-triggers-for-google-and-facebook-reviews).
- **Post Weekly Updates:** Schedule posts via HighLevel to keep your business active in Google’s eyes. [Find out how to optimize your Google Business Profile](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001222899-how-to-integrate-your-google-business-profile-formerly-gmb-into-the-crm).

---

## **2. Automate Follow-Ups & Capture Every Lead**

#### **Why This Matters**

Quick, automated responses prevent leads from going cold. Since most potential customers choose the first business that follows up, having an automated system ensures you capture every opportunity.

- **Speed is Key:** Research shows that 75% of leads book the first business that follows up.
- **Increase Bookings:** Automated follow-ups can boost your job bookings by up to 40%.

#### **What You Need to Do**

Install chat widgets, set up missed call text-back features, and deploy instant follow-up sequences (via SMS, email, or WhatsApp) to keep every inquiry engaged and moving toward a booking.

- **Install a Chat Widget:**Let customers initiate a conversation directly from your website. Follow our [chat widget setup instructions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004102-getting-started-with-chat-widget).
- **Enable Missed Call Text-Back:**If you miss a call, HighLevel can automatically text the lead, ensuring you don’t lose business. [Set up missed call text-back](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001239140-where-and-how-to-configure-the-missed-call-text-back-feature).
- **Send Instant Follow-Ups:**Automate SMS, email, and even WhatsApp messages to engage every lead.
- **Include a Booking Link:**Allow customers to schedule appointments online without waiting for a callback. [Learn how to set up online booking](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003450-recurring-appointments).
- **Deploy AI Solutions:**Use ConversationAI and Voice AI to handle routine inquiries, schedule jobs, and keep customers engaged.

  - [How to build automated appointment follow-up surveys](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001165881)
  - [How to set up Voice AI agents](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004107-creating-voice-ai-agents)
  - [How to set up Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000004401)

---

## **3. Automate Reviews & Build a Stellar Reputation**

#### **Why This Matters**

A strong portfolio of positive reviews builds trust and can significantly improve your search ranking. Customers often trust online feedback as much as personal recommendations.

- **Boost Rankings:** Electricians with 50+ Google reviews tend to rank higher and attract up to 270% more leads.
- **Trust Factor:** Approximately 90% of customers trust online reviews as much as personal recommendations.

#### **What You Need to Do**

Use automated systems to request reviews after every job, actively monitor and respond to feedback, and showcase glowing testimonials across your online channels to enhance your reputation.

- **Enable Automated Review Requests:**Configure HighLevel to send an SMS and email request after each completed job.
- **Direct Reviews to Key Platforms:**Encourage your customers to leave reviews on Google and Facebook.
- **Monitor & Respond:**Ensure you respond to all reviews—positive or negative—to build trust and improve your Google ranking.
- **Set Up Negative Review Alerts:**Catch and address negative reviews quickly before they impact your reputation.
- **Showcase Reviews:**Use HighLevel to display customer testimonials on your website and social media channels. [Learn more about reputation management](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001074-maximizing-customer-engagement-with-reviews-ai-a-guide-to-suggestive-and-auto-pilot-modes).

---

## **4. Launch a Small, High-ROI Ad Campaign**

#### **Why This Matters**

Even a modest daily ad spend can yield a steady flow of targeted leads. A well-managed ad campaign ensures that your business is seen by local homeowners actively searching for electrical services.

- **Targeted Visibility:** A well-run ad campaign ensures that your business is seen by local homeowners searching for an electrician.
- **Cost-Effective Leads:** Even a modest ad spend of $10–$20 per day can result in a steady stream of calls and bookings.

#### **What You Need to Do**

Set up and integrate targeted ad campaigns on platforms like Google Local Services and Facebook, utilize retargeting strategies, and implement call tracking to measure which ads are converting the best.

- **Set Up Google Local Services Ads (LSA):**Our step-by-step guide makes this easy.[How To Run Google LSA](https://ads.google.com/intl/en_us/home/local-services-ads/)
- **Integrate Google LSA with HighLevel:**Connect LSA with your account for seamless lead management.[How to Integrate Google LSA with HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001217374-reserve-with-google-integration-local-services-ads-lsa-)
- **Run Facebook Lead Ads:**Target local homeowners with compelling offers. [How to run Facebook ads via HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002435-create-new-ad-campaign-in-ad-manager).
- **Enable Retargeting Ads:**Continue to engage website visitors who haven’t yet booked.
- **Utilize Call Tracking in Ads:**Understand which ad is delivering the most jobs through our call tracking number pool setup. [Setting up call tracking](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000981393-how-to-set-up-call-tracking-number-pool-).

---

## **5. Stay Visible with Consistent Social Media Updates**

#### **Why This Matters**

Regular social media activity builds trust and increases your visibility, making it easier for potential customers to connect with you. Active social profiles contribute to stronger brand recognition and customer engagement.

- **Trust and Engagement:** Over 77% of homeowners check social media before hiring a contractor.
- **Boost Referrals:** Regular posts can lead to more leads and repeat business.

#### **What You Need to Do**

Develop a consistent posting schedule across platforms, share engaging visual content such as before-and-after photos or testimonials, and use automation tools to maintain your online presence effortlessly.

- **Post Regular Updates on Google Business:**Keep your profile active to maintain higher search rankings.
- **Share Visual Content on Facebook & Instagram:**Post before-and-after job photos, customer testimonials, and time-lapse videos of your work. [Guide to sharing reviews on social media](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001620-share-your-reviews-as-posts-on-social-media-using-social-planner).
- **Start a Blog or Newsletter:**Provide electrical safety tips, energy efficiency advice, and home upgrade ideas.
  - [How to Create a Blog](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002448-how-to-create-a-blog-)
  - [How to Set Up an RSS Feed for Blogs](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001231723-how-to-set-up-an-rss-feed-for-blogs)

title_en: Knowledge Base Web Crawler Sitemap-Powered URL Selection
source_md:
Knowledge Base

# Knowledge Base Web Crawler Sitemap-Powered URL Selection

Choose exactly which website pages to train into your Knowledge Base with sitemap preview, live quota tracking, and full discovery crawl options

What You'll Learn

This guide explains how sitemap-powered URL selection gives you precise control over which website pages are trained into your HighLevel Knowledge Base. You'll learn how the sitemap preview modal, discovery crawl, and URL quota tools make web training faster, clearer, and more efficient.

By the end of this article, you'll be able to preview discovered URLs, curate exactly which pages to train, monitor crawl and training progress with live operation cards, and recover from failed URLs without re-running entire crawls.

## What is Sitemap-Powered URL Selection?

Sitemap-powered URL selection is an updated Web Crawler workflow that lets you preview and select website pages before training them into a Knowledge Base. When HighLevel finds sitemap URLs for a website, the "Select Pages to Train" modal displays available pages so you can choose only the URLs that should be used as Knowledge Base content.

This is useful when a website has many pages, but only some pages are relevant for AI answers. You can search, paginate, select individual URLs, review available page quota, and train selected pages from one modal. If a needed page is missing from the sitemap results, "Discover by Crawling" can be used as a fallback to find pages by following links from the website.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078015126/original/dZeAViOdCQZcQQlTHrIgbb4TNf-soWz-2g.png?1786360429)

## Key Benefits

Choosing specific website pages gives you better control over what your Knowledge Base learns from. This helps reduce irrelevant content, avoid unnecessary page usage, and make website training easier to monitor.

**Precise page selection** — Choose the exact website URLs you want to train instead of training pages blindly.

**Faster setup** — Use sitemap results, search, pagination, and row controls to find relevant pages quickly.

**Better quota visibility** — Review how many pages are selected and how many pages are available before training.

**Fallback discovery** — Use "Discover by Crawling" when sitemap results are missing pages.

**Clearer progress tracking** — Monitor crawling and training progress from the operation card.

**Manual retry support** — Retry failed URLs when training does not complete successfully.

## Where to Find the Web Crawler

The Web Crawler is available inside a Knowledge Base and is used to train website content. Website sources can help AI tools answer questions using selected public website pages.

To find the Web Crawler:

- Go to **AI Agents** in HighLevel
- Open **Knowledge Base**
- Select the Knowledge Base you want to update
- Click the **Web Crawler** tab
- Click **Add Website** to add a new website source

The Web Crawler tab shows website sources, trained page statuses, updated timestamps, and page-level actions.

## URL Selection Modes

URL selection modes determine how HighLevel looks for pages related to the URL you enter. Choosing the right mode helps narrow the page list before selecting URLs to train.

Exact URL

Single-page training

Uses a specific page URL. Ideal for training one specific page without browsing a larger list.

All URLs with this Path

Path-based discovery

Finds pages under a specific website path (e.g., /help, /docs, /support). Helpful when only a specific section should be used for Knowledge Base training.

All URLs in this Domain

Domain-wide discovery

Finds pages across the selected domain. Ideal when most of your site is relevant (e.g., documentation sites, small marketing websites). The sitemap modal lets you deselect irrelevant sub-areas.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078015306/original/W6fT1aG_c-97NewgeO6eoGOAtnBHSFOYZw.png?1786360499)

## Select Pages to Train Modal

The "Select Pages to Train" modal is the core interface for sitemap-powered URL selection. It surfaces all discovered URLs in a structured table so you can quickly review, filter, and choose which pages belong in your Knowledge Base before any training occurs.

Within this modal, you can move from "train everything" to a deliberate, curated set of URLs—especially important for large or complex sites where only some pages are relevant to customers.

Modal Features

What you'll see in the modal

The modal includes:

- Sitemap-found page count (e.g., "Sitemap found — 426 pages")
- Selected page counter (e.g., "0 selected of 3995 available")
- Search field to filter URLs by keyword or path
- Individual page checkboxes for selection
- Select-all option to quickly choose all listed URLs
- Rows per page selector (e.g., 10, 25, 50)
- Pagination controls to navigate large lists
- "Discover by Crawling" button for deeper discovery
- "Train Selected" button to start training chosen URLs

Performance

UI performance improvements

Changing the page number, adjusting the number of rows per page, or updating the search query refreshes only the URL list. The modal itself stays open and responsive while you work through long lists (thousands of URLs) in just a few seconds.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078015416/original/LBvHnYb9kzJ7reO3lRqKj4_-KN1vsC2WSg.png?1786360556)

## Page Quota Counter

The quota counter helps prevent surprises before training begins. It shows how many pages are selected and how many pages are available for training based on the Knowledge Base limit.

Managing your URL quota is crucial for a healthy Knowledge Base. HighLevel lets you train up to a fixed number of web URLs per Knowledge Base (such as 4,000 URLs) and tracks which URLs are already part of your training data. The live quota counter keeps you within this limit without guesswork.

Counter Behavior

How the quota counter works

The counter displays a running tally such as "120 of 3,995 available".

It updates instantly as you:

- Select or deselect URLs in the modal
- Include or exclude previously trained URLs

The counter automatically accounts for URLs already present in your Knowledge Base, showing how much capacity remains for new pages.

Benefits

Practical benefits

- Avoids mid-training errors caused by exceeding your URL limit
- Encourages curating only high-value URLs instead of training entire domains by default
- Makes it easy to plan for future additions, reserving quota for new product pages or documentation

## Discover by Crawling

"Discover by Crawling" is a fallback option when sitemap results are missing pages or when the sitemap does not include everything you need. Instead of relying only on sitemap results, this option follows links from the website to discover additional pages.

This option pairs with the Enhanced Web Crawler's advanced link discovery, which supports recursive sitemap crawling, zipped sitemap files, and dynamic link detection.

When to Use

When to use "Discover by Crawling"

- The page you need is missing from the sitemap list
- Your site has no sitemap or an incomplete sitemap
- Key pages are only accessible through navigation menus, accordions, or other interactive elements
- You've recently added new sections that aren't yet reflected in the sitemap
- You want maximum coverage up to your URL limit

Behavior

How "Discover by Crawling" works

- Starts from your domain or path seed and follows internal links within the allowed scope
- Respects navigation boundaries and root-domain rules to prevent crawler drift
- Updates the URL list in the modal as additional pages are discovered
- Operation cards show progress like "Crawling — 42 pages found so far"
- May take longer than sitemap-powered selection because it explores links actively

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078016082/original/cV5ba1EjCiBUxlr5DdDfO2dTH9IiuoS7uw.png?1786360972)

## Monitor Crawling and Training Progress

Operation cards give you real-time visibility into what the Web Crawler is doing and how your training run is progressing. This transparency is especially important for large sites or deep discovery crawls.

Rather than leaving you guessing, the UI surfaces status messages and counts that persist across page refreshes and tab switches.

Card Content

What operation cards typically show

- Crawling progress with status messages
- Training progress (e.g., "Training 5 of 5")
- Number of pages found during crawling
- Number of pages trained successfully
- Current operation status (in progress, completed, or failed)
- Visual progress indicators showing completion percentage

Importance

Why this matters

- You can safely navigate away from the page or switch tabs without interrupting the crawl or losing visibility
- When troubleshooting, you can quickly see whether issues happened during discovery, training, or both
- Non-technical team members get an easy, readable view of "what's happening now" with Knowledge Base training

## Retry Failed URLs

Not every URL will train successfully on the first attempt—pages can time out, respond slowly, or temporarily fail due to external conditions. Manual retry tools let you recover from these failures without re-running the entire crawl.

The operation results provide a reliable way to identify and selectively retry problem pages.

Retry Process

How manual retry works

If a page fails during crawling or training:

- Open the Knowledge Base and go to the Web Crawler tab
- Review the website source or page list for failed URLs
- Use the page-level retry or refresh action when available
- Monitor the operation card until the retry completes

Best Practices

Best practices for handling failures

Check the URL itself first

Verify the page loads correctly in a browser (no 404s, redirect loops, or login walls).

Retry in smaller batches

If multiple URLs failed, try retraining a subset to spot patterns.

Combine with Auto Refresh

Once URLs are successfully trained, you can enable Auto Refresh to keep them updated automatically.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078016160/original/DeHV5QQkLq6BgZ2QGCKSYjoFj62XwI5Q0w.png?1786361026)

## How to Train Website Pages Using Sitemap-Powered URL Selection

Proper setup ensures your Knowledge Base trains only the pages that are useful for AI answers. Start by selecting a website source, choose the right URL mode, and review the sitemap-powered page list before training.

Step 1

Open Your Knowledge Base

- Go to **AI Agents → Knowledge Base** in your sub-account
- Open an existing Knowledge Base or create a new one
- Select the **Web Crawler** tab

Step 2

Add a Website Source

- Click **+ Add Website**
- Choose the URL selection mode:
  - Exact URL (for single pages)
  - All URLs with this Path (for path-based training)
  - All URLs in this Domain (for domain-wide training)
- Enter the starting URL (including https://)
- Click **Select Pages to Train**

Step 3

Review the Sitemap Preview Modal

- HighLevel fetches the sitemap and displays discovered URLs
- The modal shows the sitemap-found page count (e.g., "Sitemap found — 426 pages")
- Review the URL list to see what pages are available

Step 4

Search, Filter, and Select URLs

- Use the search bar to find URLs by keyword or path
- Adjust rows per page if working with a large site
- Navigate with pagination controls to browse the full list
- Check boxes next to URLs you want to train
- Use the "Select all" checkbox for bulk selection when appropriate
- Deselect any irrelevant URLs
- Watch the quota counter (e.g., "120 of 3,995 available") to stay under your limit

Step 5 (Optional)

Run Discover by Crawling

If needed pages are missing from the sitemap or your sitemap is incomplete:

- Click **Discover by Crawling**
- Allow the crawler time to explore internal links
- As new URLs appear in the table, refine selections using search and checkboxes
- Monitor the operation card for crawl progress messages

Step 6

Train the Selected URLs

- Confirm your URL selections and verify the quota counter
- Click **Train Selected**
- An operation card appears showing training progress
- You can safely navigate to other tabs—the operation continues in the background

Step 7

Review Results and Retry Failed URLs

- Once training completes, review the trained URL list
- Check for any failed URLs
- If URLs failed, use the page-level retry/refresh action when available
- Test your Knowledge Base using the retrieval tester to confirm content is retrievable

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What is sitemap-powered URL selection?

A: It is a Web Crawler workflow that shows available website URLs from a sitemap so you can choose which pages to train into the Knowledge Base.

Q: Does sitemap-powered URL selection change my URL limit per Knowledge Base?

No. Your overall per-Knowledge Base URL limit remains the same (for example, up to 4,000 web URLs). The new experience simply makes it easier to see how many URLs you have left and avoid overshooting the limit while selecting pages.

Q: When should I use sitemap preview vs. "Discover by Crawling"?

Use the sitemap preview when your website's sitemap is accurate and covers the sections you care about—this is usually faster and lighter. Use "Discover by Crawling" when you suspect the sitemap is missing sections, your site is highly dynamic, or important content is only reachable through navigation and interactive components.

Q: Can I search the list of pages before training?

Yes. Use the search field in the "Select Pages to Train" modal to find specific pages or URL paths.

Q: Can I select all pages at once?

Yes. Use the "Select all" checkbox in the modal. Review your available quota before training all pages.

title_en: How to Connect AI Clients to Project Management with MCP
source_md:
HighLevel Project Management now connects with compatible AI assistants through Model Context Protocol (MCP), making it easier to organize and manage project work using natural language. With this integration, you can create and update tasks, subtasks, Spaces, and Lists without switching between your AI client and HighLevel. You can also work with custom statuses, custom field values, and task comments through an authorized connection. This guide covers how to connect a supported AI client using OAuth and start managing Project Management work through MCP.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Project Management MCP?](#What-is-Project-Management-MCP?)
- [Key Benefits of Project Management MCP](#Key-Benefits-of-Project-Management-MCP)
- [How To Setup Project Management MCP](#How-To-Setup-Project-Management-MCP)
- [Connect Your AI Client](#Connect-Your-AI-Client)
  - [Authorize Your Connection with OAuth](#Authorize-Your-Connection-with-OAuth)
  - [Send Your First Project Management Request](#Send-Your-First-Project-Management-Request)
- [Manage Project Work Using Natural Language](#Manage-Project-Work-Using-Natural-Language)
  - [Create and Update Tasks, Subtasks, Spaces, and Lists](#Create-and-Update-Tasks,-Subtasks,-Spaces,-and-Lists)
  - [Work with Custom Statuses and Fields](#Work-with-Custom-Statuses-and-Fields)
  - [Read and Post Task Comments](#Read-and-Post-Task-Comments)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
  - [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Project Management MCP?**

Project Management MCP is an integration that connects compatible AI clients to HighLevel Project Management through Model Context Protocol (MCP). MCP allows an AI assistant to discover and use supported HighLevel operations through a standardized connection.

Instead of opening Project Management whenever you need to create tasks, organize Lists, or review comments, you can describe the action in your connected AI client.

The integration supports creating and managing tasks, subtasks, Spaces, and Lists. It also supports working with custom statuses, custom field values, and task comments.

Connections use a hosted MCP endpoint and OAuth authentication. You authorize the connection through your own account rather than configuring shared credentials or building directly against the Projects REST API.

**Supported AI Clients**

- Claude.ai
- ChatGPT
- Cursor
- Codex
- Claude Code
- Muse

---

## **Key Benefits of Project Management MCP**

Project Management MCP helps you manage project work from your AI assistant while keeping that work inside HighLevel. Natural-language instructions reduce routine navigation and provide another way to interact with project information.

- **Natural-language task management:** Create and update tasks, subtasks, Spaces, and Lists by describing the work you want to complete.

- **Less context switching:** Manage supported project activities without repeatedly opening the Project Management interface.

- **Custom statuses and fields:** Create tasks with appropriate statuses and custom field values, reducing manual adjustments after creation.

- **Task discussions:** Read task comments and post new comments through your connected AI client.

- **Simplified integration:** Use hosted MCP connectivity to work with supported project operations without building directly against the Projects REST API.

- **OAuth-based authentication:** Connect through your own authorization and grant access to the requested HighLevel resources.

- **No local server setup:** The hosted endpoint does not require a locally installed MCP server or VPN connection.

---

## **How To Setup Project Management MCP**

Connecting Project Management to an AI assistant involves configuring a hosted MCP connection and completing OAuth authorization. Once connected, you can use natural-language requests to work with supported project resources.

The initial connection process starts inside your AI client. HighLevel authentication takes place when the client begins the OAuth authorization flow.

### 

### **Connect Your AI Client**

Choose the MCP endpoint associated with your AI client. The following endpoints are documented in HighLevel's MCP resources.

| AI Client | Hosted MCP Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Claude.ai | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2` |
| Claude Code | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2` |
| ChatGPT | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/` |
| Codex | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/` |
| Muse | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/muse/v2/` |

**Connect ChatGPT**

ChatGPT supports a dedicated OAuth-based MCP connection. You can configure the connection as a custom MCP app when your ChatGPT account and workspace permissions allow it.

1. Open ChatGPT on the web.
2. Open **Settings**.
3. Select **Apps**.
4. If your account requires Developer mode, enable it before creating the MCP connection.
5. Select **Create** to begin creating a custom MCP app.
6. Enter a name for the connection, such as **HighLevel Project Management**.
7. Add a description identifying the connection as your HighLevel MCP integration.
8. Enter the following MCP server URL:

   `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/`
9. Continue with the MCP app configuration.
10. Select the available option to scan or discover the MCP tools.
11. Begin OAuth authorization when prompted.
12. After completing authorization, return to ChatGPT and finish creating the app.

**Connect Claude.ai**

Claude.ai supports HighLevel MCP connections through a custom connector. After adding the hosted endpoint, complete OAuth authorization to make the approved HighLevel operations available.

1. Open Claude.ai.
2. Select **Settings**.
3. Select **Connectors**.
4. Click **Add custom connector**.
5. Enter the following server URL:

   `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2`
6. Click **Connect**.
7. Complete the HighLevel OAuth authorization process.
8. Start a new Claude conversation after the connection is established.

**Connect Codex**

Codex supports the OpenAI-compatible MCP endpoint through its CLI or supported IDE extension.

To connect using the Codex IDE extension:

1. Open the Codex IDE extension.
2. Select the **gear** menu.
3. Select **MCP servers**.
4. Click **Add server**.
5. Choose **Streamable HTTP**.
6. Enter the following server URL:

   `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/`
7. Select **Authenticate**.
8. Complete the HighLevel OAuth authorization process.

For Codex CLI, add the server using:

`codex mcp add leadconnector --url https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/`

Then begin OAuth authentication:

`codex mcp login leadconnector`

Follow the sign-in and authorization prompts.

**Connect Claude Code**

Claude Code supports the Anthropic-specific endpoint through its MCP configuration.

1. Open your terminal.
2. Add the hosted MCP server using:

   `claude mcp add --transport http leadconnector https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2`
3. Complete the HighLevel OAuth authorization process when the browser opens.
4. Verify the connection using:

   `claude mcp list`

**Connect Muse**

Muse provides HighLevel MCP as an official app. Its connection uses the Muse-specific endpoint and OAuth authentication.

1. Open Muse.
2. Locate the app or MCP connection options.
3. Select the HighLevel app.
4. Begin the connection process.
5. Complete the HighLevel OAuth authorization flow.
6. Return to Muse and confirm that HighLevel is connected.

### **Authorize Your Connection with OAuth**

OAuth allows your AI client to access approved HighLevel resources without requiring a shared account credential. During authorization, you select the available sub-account access and review the permissions requested by the connection.

1. Begin the OAuth authorization process from your AI client.
2. When the HighLevel authorization page opens, sign in with your HighLevel credentials.
3. Select the sub-account you want to connect.
4. If an eligible agency connection offers multi-sub-account access, select the appropriate sub-accounts.
5. Review the OAuth scopes and permissions requested by the integration.
6. Approve the authorization request.
7. Return to your AI client after authentication completes.
8. Confirm that the HighLevel MCP connection appears as connected.

### 

### **Send Your First Project Management Request**

Once your AI client is connected, you can describe the project work you want to manage. Start with a specific request that identifies the target List, the required action, and the relevant task details.

1. Open your connected AI client.
2. Start a new conversation or use an existing conversation with the HighLevel MCP connection available.
3. For clients that require manual tool selection, select the connected HighLevel MCP app or tool.
4. Enter a natural-language request.

   **Example:**

   "Create three tasks in the Onboarding List, due Friday, assigned to me."
5. Review the AI client's response and any operation results.
6. Verify the resulting tasks in HighLevel Project Management.

To verify the tasks in HighLevel:

1. Open HighLevel and switch to the relevant **Sub-Account** view.
2. Select **Contacts** from the left navigation menu.
3. Select the **Tasks** tab at the top of the page.
4. In the **Spaces** panel on the left, expand the relevant Space.
5. Select the **Onboarding** List.
6. Review the tasks and their assigned details.

## 

## **Manage Project Work Using Natural Language**

Once connected, your AI assistant can help with supported Project Management activities. You can describe the work you want to complete without manually navigating through every project action.

The following examples illustrate the supported capabilities identified in this release. Actual execution depends on the operations available to your connection and the permissions you approve.

### 

### **Create and Update Tasks, Subtasks, Spaces, and Lists**

Project Management organizes work through Spaces, optional Folders, Lists, tasks, and subtasks. MCP allows compatible AI clients to create and manage supported project objects using natural-language instructions.

You can request actions such as:

- Creating a new Space for a team or work stream.
- Creating a List inside a Space.
- Creating tasks in a selected List.
- Updating existing tasks.
- Creating or updating subtasks under a parent task.

**Example request:**

"Create a new Space for Client Onboarding and add an Onboarding List."

### 

### **Work with Custom Statuses and Fields**

Custom statuses help teams organize tasks by workflow stage, while custom fields store additional information relevant to a project.

Project Management MCP supports creating tasks with appropriate statuses and custom field values. This helps reduce the manual adjustments required after creating a task.

**Example request:**

"Create a task in the Onboarding List with the status and custom field values I specify."

For accurate results, reference the appropriate status and custom field values when describing the task.

### 

### **Read and Post Task Comments**

Task comments allow team members to discuss project work and keep important context alongside the relevant task.

With Project Management MCP, you can ask your AI client to read existing task comments or post a new comment. This lets you review discussions and contribute updates without opening the task interface.

**Example requests:**

- "Read the comments on the client onboarding task."
- "Add a comment to the client onboarding task with the latest project update."

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do I need to create a Private Integration Token to connect Project Management MCP?**

No. The dedicated OAuth endpoints documented for Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, and Muse use a sign-in and authorization flow. These connections do not require you to manually create a Private Integration Token.

The older general-purpose MCP setup guide also documents token-based connections. Follow the authentication method appropriate for your selected endpoint.

**Q: Can an agency connect multiple HighLevel sub-accounts to the same AI client?**

Agency multi-sub-account connections are supported where the applicable installation option is available. During authorization, an agency can select the sub-accounts the connection may access.

Every request operates against one authorized sub-account at a time. Multi-sub-account availability is being rolled out and may not appear for every installation.

**Q: Can I revoke an AI client's access to HighLevel after connecting it?**

Yes. HighLevel's OAuth MCP documentation supports reviewing and revoking authorized connection access.

Revoking authorization removes the permissions previously granted to that connection.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Introduction to Project Management](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008442-introduction-to-project-management)

- [Organize work with Spaces, Folders, and Lists](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008443-organize-work-with-spaces-folders-and-lists)

- [Create a task or subtask](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008444-create-a-task-or-subtask)

- [Connect ChatGPT and Codex to LeadConnector MCP](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009114-connect-chatgpt-and-codex-to-leadconnector-mcp)

- [HighLevel MCP Multi-Account Support for Claude](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008360-highlevel-mcp-multi-account-support-for-claude)

- [Connect HighLevel MCP to Muse](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009042-connect-highlevel-mcp-to-muse)

title_en: Pre-Built A2P Campaign Registration with Chat Widget
source_md:
SMS Compliance

# Pre-Built A2P Campaign (Widget-First) Registration

Complete Campaign Registration with Chat Widget Setup using HighLevel's guided flow, auto-generated consent widget, and support for Marketing, Informational, and Mixed messaging programs.

What You'll Learn

HighLevel's Pre-Built A2P Campaign (Widget-First) flow uses a guided questionnaire and an auto-generated Chat Widget to help you complete Campaign registration with built-in compliance safeguards.

This guide covers the widget-first approach, Marketing, Informational, and Mixed messaging use cases, the generated consent experience, and step-by-step instructions for registering your Campaign.

## What is the Pre-Built A2P Campaign (Widget-First) Flow?

The Pre-Built A2P Campaign (Widget-First) flow uses a HighLevel-generated Chat Widget and guided Campaign setup to simplify SMS consent configuration. Campaign registration opens in **Chat Widget Setup** by default. If your business already collects SMS consent using another approved method, you can switch to **Manual Setup**.

Chat Widget Setup supports **Marketing / Promotional**, **Informational / Non-Marketing**, and **Mixed** messaging programs. Mixed is designed for one messaging program that includes both promotional and informational communication.

![Pre-built campaign registration flow selection showing Chat Widget as recommended option](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077192716/original/gejxJhX9MYE3MM4aA0E1jlnBsrmJWoKl1w.png?1785385543)

## Key Benefits

The widget-first registration flow includes built-in safeguards that help simplify consent configuration, align Campaign details with the live opt-in experience, and reduce avoidable compliance issues compared with a fully manual submission.

**Guided Setup:** Carrier-safe disclosure language is filled in automatically, so you do not need to write compliance text yourself.

**Mixed Messaging Support:** Businesses that send both promotional and informational messages can use the guided Chat Widget flow while collecting the two consent types independently.

**Fewer Avoidable Issues:** Financial and marketing conflicts are flagged before submission, which is designed to reduce a common cause of Campaign rejection.

**Automatic Age-Gating:** When required by your Campaign content, a mandatory Date of Birth field is added to the widget to support CTIA compliance.

**No Manual Disclaimers:** STOP/HELP text, frequency notices, and data rate disclosures are system-generated and cannot be edited or removed.

**Consistent Compliance Fields:** Compliance-sensitive fields are locked, which helps keep what carriers review aligned with what goes live on your website.

## Understanding the Pre-Built Campaign Flow

The widget-first flow includes automated guardrails and pre-configured components that help keep your Campaign details, consent experience, and messaging purpose aligned with carrier requirements.

Feature 1

Simplified Messaging Use Case Selection

At the start of registration, select the messaging category that matches your program:

- **Marketing / Promotional** for promotional messaging.
- **Informational / Non-Marketing** for transactional or informational messaging.
- **Mixed** when the same messaging program includes both categories.

For Marketing and Informational selections, the Campaign Use Case options are filtered to match the selected messaging category. When **Mixed** is selected, the Campaign Use Case is automatically set to **Low Volume Mixed**.

Feature 2

Financial + Marketing Conflict Check

If you select **Marketing / Promotional** and also indicate that your Campaign involves financial services or loan-related content, the flow prompts you to switch to **Informational** before continuing. This helps prevent a high-risk combination that carriers commonly reject.

Feature 3

Automatic Age-Gating

When you indicate that your Campaign involves age-gated content and/or financial services or loan-related content, the widget automatically adds a mandatory **Date of Birth** field. Contacts cannot submit the form without confirming they meet the minimum age requirement, which supports CTIA rules for restricted categories.

Feature 4

Auto-Generated Chat Widget

HighLevel automatically creates a brand-specific widget that includes your business name, frequency disclosure, "Msg & data rates may apply" notice, and STOP/HELP instructions. HighLevel also generates the JavaScript embed code for your website.

If **Mixed** is selected, the generated widget includes two independent consent checkboxes: one for informational/transactional messaging and one for marketing/promotional messaging. Neither checkbox is pre-selected, and each consent choice includes its own system-controlled disclosure content.

You can adjust colors and header text only. Disclosure language, required fields, and consent checkboxes cannot be edited or removed, so the live widget matches what was submitted for review.

![Auto-generated chat widget code with compliance disclosures embedded](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077193544/original/ie0gyNyv1d5xlJxllpiaVTFzICQO-LmGvg.png?1785387958)

Feature 5

Locked Consent Review Screen

Before submission, you review a read-only summary that includes your consent fields, system-generated sample messages, and your opt-in method. These fields are non-editable, which helps keep your registration details consistent with the live widget.

![Chat widget preview showing form fields including name, phone, date of birth, and consent text](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077192893/original/PglLOrZ2zFfEdDw8v5CPnZjGoNPCzqUBWg.png?1785386328)

## How to Set Up a Pre-Built A2P Campaign

Before You Start

Before you begin, make sure the following are in place:

- Your A2P Brand registration is approved, or eligible to continue.
- Your business has a live, publicly accessible website.
- The website represents the same business submitted during Brand registration.
- The website includes a Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions.
- You know whether your messaging program is Marketing / Promotional, Informational / Non-Marketing, or Mixed.

Follow these steps to register your Campaign using the widget-first flow. Selecting the correct messaging category is important because it determines the available Campaign use case and the consent structure generated for the widget.

Step 1

Access Campaign Registration

In your sub-account, go to **Settings → Phone System → Trust Center**. Under **A2P Messaging (SMS)**, continue to Campaign registration. If you are creating an additional Campaign, go to **Brand & Campaigns → Campaigns → Create Campaign**.

Step 2

Continue to Chat Widget Setup

After Brand registration is complete, Campaign registration opens in **Chat Widget Setup** by default. Complete the Chat Widget Setup fields to configure the consent experience for your Campaign.

Use **Manual Setup** if you already collect SMS consent through another approved method, such as an existing website form, paper form, lead form, QR code, kiosk, or verbal consent. Select **Switch to Manual Setup** below the first Chat Widget Setup screen.

**Note:** If you switch to Manual Setup and decide to use the Chat Widget instead, select **Chat Widget Setup — recommended** from the Campaign details step panel.

![Registration flow selection screen with Pre-built campaign option highlighted](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077192716/original/gejxJhX9MYE3MM4aA0E1jlnBsrmJWoKl1w.png?1785385543)

Step 3

Choose Your Messaging Use Case

Select the option that accurately represents the messaging program:

- **Marketing / Promotional:** Select this when your Campaign sends promotional offers, advertising, discounts, newsletters, or similar marketing content.
- **Informational / Non-Marketing:** Select this when your Campaign sends transactional or informational communication such as reminders, confirmations, and service updates.
- **Mixed:** Select this when the same messaging program genuinely includes both promotional and informational messaging.

When **Mixed** is selected, HighLevel automatically sets the **Campaign Use Case** to **Low Volume Mixed**.

![Mixed messaging use case selected with Low Volume Mixed automatically assigned as the Campaign Use Case](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080734379/original/dOFPBjxJHMgPsl4iMkGeakQvOcv2LlND3w.png?1789140163)

Step 4

Answer the Guided Questionnaire

Respond to questions about your Campaign content, including whether it involves financial services, loan-related content, or age-gated materials. If you select a disallowed combination, such as Marketing plus Financial, the flow prompts you to adjust your selections before continuing.

Step 5

Review and Customize the Widget

Preview the auto-generated Chat Widget. You can adjust colors and header text, but disclosure language, required fields including any mandatory Date of Birth field, and consent notices are locked and cannot be modified.

If **Mixed** is selected, verify that the widget displays a separate informational/transactional consent checkbox and a separate marketing/promotional consent checkbox. Neither option should be pre-selected, and each consent choice should display its associated disclosure content.

![Generated Mixed Chat Widget showing separate informational and promotional SMS consent checkboxes](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080734457/original/M7RLGjH-ASALiZplsDQN9UF-qrrXV2L2Vw.png?1789140188)

Step 6

Copy and Install the Widget on Your Website

Copy the provided JavaScript embed code and install it on the web page you confirmed during setup. The widget needs to be live and publicly viewable before you complete the compliance check in the next step.

**Important:** The Chat Widget should be the only form on the submitted page collecting SMS consent. Do not place another SMS opt-in form, such as a Contact Form, Lead Capture Form, or Appointment Form, on the same page.

Step 7

Complete the Website Compliance Check

Confirm that your website meets carrier and platform requirements. Your submitted website should:

- Be live and publicly accessible.
- Clearly represent the registered business.
- Match the business information used during Brand registration.
- Display appropriate business/contact information.
- Include a Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions.
- Have the required SMS opt-in experience available on the submitted page.

![User consent screen with compliance checklist and sample message fields](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155077192889/original/yMxbG9nvvaajdi1qkiKQooVe75_fdCFgMQ.png?1785386304)

Step 8

Review the Application and Submit

Click **Review Application** to run the compliance review. If HighLevel identifies an issue, review the recommendation, correct the applicable Campaign or website information, and run the review again. Once the required checks pass, submit the Campaign for carrier review. Passing the HighLevel review does not guarantee carrier approval — the final decision is made by carriers and registration partners.

Step 9

Monitor Campaign Status

Go to **Campaigns → Status** to track your submission. Review times can vary, so check the status in Trust Center rather than creating a duplicate Campaign.

Campaign Submitted

Your Campaign has been submitted for carrier review. You can begin sending SMS once approval is confirmed.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What happens if I select Mixed as my messaging use case?

Selecting Mixed automatically sets the Campaign use case to **Low Volume Mixed**. The generated Chat Widget includes separate consent choices for informational/transactional and marketing/promotional SMS.

Q: Can a contact choose only one consent type in a Mixed widget?

Yes. The two consent checkboxes are independent. A contact can opt into informational messaging only, marketing messaging only, or both. Neither checkbox is pre-selected.

Q: Can I customize the auto-generated Chat Widget?

You can adjust appearance elements such as colors and header text. Compliance-sensitive elements — disclosure language, required fields, and consent checkboxes — are locked and cannot be edited or removed, so the live widget matches your registration.

Q: When should I use Manual Setup instead of Chat Widget Setup?

Use Manual Setup if your business already collects SMS consent through another approved method, such as an existing website form, paper form, lead form, QR code, kiosk, or verbal consent. Chat Widget Setup remains the recommended default option.

Q: Does the Date of Birth field appear on every widget?

No. The Date of Birth field only appears when you indicate during setup that your Campaign involves age-gated content and/or financial services or loan-related content. When required, the field is locked into the widget and cannot be removed.

Q: Does the Chat Widget need to be installed before I submit my Campaign?

Yes. The widget should be live and publicly accessible on the submitted page before you run the compliance review and complete final submission. Carriers require the opt-in method to be viewable at the URL you provide during registration.

Q: What should I do if the compliance review finds an issue?

Review the recommendation shown in the modal, correct the applicable Campaign or website information, and run the review again. Submit the Campaign for carrier review only after the required checks pass.

title_en: Phone Number Change Security Alerts and Reversal
source_md:
A user’s phone number is an important account security field because it may be used to receive login security codes and two-factor authentication codes. HighLevel now provides proactive security notifications when a user’s phone number is added or changed, helping users recognize unexpected account updates quickly. When an existing phone number is changed, eligible alerts also provide a secure, self-service way to restore the previous number. These safeguards give users greater visibility and control over security-sensitive profile changes.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Phone Number Change Security Alerts and Reversal?](#What-are-Phone-Number-Change-Security-Alerts-and-Reversal?)
- [Key Benefits of Phone Number Change Security Alerts and Reversal](#Key-Benefits-of-Phone-Number-Change-Security-Alerts-and-Reversal)
- [How Phone Number Security Notifications Work](#How-Phone-Number-Security-Notifications-Work)
- [Phone Number Changes Made by an Admin](#Phone-Number-Changes-Made-by-an-Admin)
- [Reversing an Unexpected Phone Number Change](#Reversing-an-Unexpected-Phone-Number-Change)
- [Security Alerts and White-Label Agencies](#Security-Alerts-and-White-Label-Agencies)
- [Phone Number Changes and Two-Factor Authentication](#Phone-Number-Changes-and-Two-Factor-Authentication)
- [Auditability of Phone Number Reversals](#Auditability-of-Phone-Number-Reversals)
- [How To Use Phone Number Change Security Alerts and Reversal](#How-To-Use-Phone-Number-Change-Security-Alerts-and-Reversal)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What are Phone Number Change Security Alerts and Reversal?**

Phone Number Change Security Alerts notify the affected user when their phone number is added or changed in HighLevel. These alerts help users verify whether the update was expected and identify whether the change was made by them or by an administrator. When an existing phone number is changed, the security alert includes a single-use reversal link that can restore the previous number without requiring the user to log in.

Phone numbers are security-sensitive because they may be used for identity verification and account access. HighLevel also uses additional safeguards, including verification requirements for sensitive user-account changes, so these notifications provide an additional layer of visibility after the update occurs.

When a phone number is added or changed, the affected user receives a security alert through supported notification channels.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081732091/original/XE5I6XQGnEGGRmbhWoqFuJPAWMlsCECvcg.png?1790240625)  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081732211/original/hpr1R2IZPWRCNKhLohoC3noqRjHQ485lgg.png?1790240660)

For a phone number change, notifications can include:

- Email notification
- In-app notification
- SMS notification sent to the previous phone number

The notification identifies:

- What information changed
- When the change occurred, displayed in the user’s timezone
- Whether the change was initiated **by you** or **by your admin**
- What action to take if the change was unexpected

---

## **Key Benefits of Phone Number Change Security Alerts and Reversal**

Phone-number security notifications give users immediate awareness of changes to an account field that may affect authentication and account access. The reversal option also reduces reliance on administrator or support intervention when an existing number was changed unexpectedly.

- **Immediate visibility:** Users are proactively notified when their phone number is added or changed.
- **Multiple notification channels:** Alerts can reach the affected user through email, in-app notifications, and, for phone-number changes, SMS to the previous number.
- **Clear change attribution:** Users can see whether the update was made by them or by an administrator.
- **Self-service recovery:** An unexpected phone-number change can be reversed using a single-use link.
- **No login required for reversal:** Users can restore the previous phone number even if the change affected their normal authentication flow.
- **Time-limited protection:** The reversal link remains valid for 7 days.
- **White-label support:** Security alerts use the agency’s branding and domain rather than HighLevel branding.
- **Auditability:** Phone-number reversals are recorded so security-sensitive activity can be traced.

---

## **How Phone Number Security Notifications Work**

Security notifications are designed to make sensitive phone-number changes visible to the person whose account information was updated. The notification method depends on whether a number is being added for the first time or an existing number is being replaced.

When a user’s phone number is added or changed, HighLevel generates a security alert for the affected user.

For an existing phone-number change:

- An email security alert is sent.
- An in-app security notification is generated.
- An SMS security alert is sent to the **previous phone number**.
- The alert provides information about when and how the change occurred.
- A reversal link is included so the previous phone number can be restored if necessary.

Sending an SMS to the previous number is especially important because it gives the person who previously controlled that number an opportunity to recognize and respond to an unexpected change.

If the change was expected, the user does not need to take any action.

---

## **Phone Number Changes Made by an Admin**

Administrator-initiated changes receive the same security visibility as changes made directly by users. This helps ensure that users remain informed when an administrator updates security-sensitive profile information on their behalf.

HighLevel supports user management at both the agency and sub-account levels. Agency users can be managed from **Agency View > Settings > Team**, while sub-account users can be managed from **Sub-Account > Settings > My Staff**. Existing user-management controls allow authorized users to edit profile information such as a user’s phone number.

When an administrator changes another user’s phone number, the security alert identifies the action as being performed **by your admin**.

This allows the affected user to distinguish an administrator-initiated change from one they performed themselves.

Security alerts also cover supported admin-impersonation and user-management flows where a phone number is changed on the user’s behalf.

---

## **Reversing an Unexpected Phone Number Change**

The reversal link provides a direct recovery path when an existing phone number was changed unexpectedly. Because the reversal does not require a HighLevel login, users can act even when the updated number may interfere with their normal authentication process.

Each eligible security alert includes a **single-use reversal link**.

The link:

- Is valid for **7 days**
- Can be used only once
- Does not require the user to log in
- Restores the previous phone number
- Displays a confirmation after the reversal is completed

If the phone-number change was expected, no action is required.

If the change was unexpected:

1. Open the security alert.
2. Review the change details to verify when the phone number was changed and who initiated the update.
3. Click the reversal link in the alert.
4. HighLevel restores the previous phone number.
5. Review the confirmation page to verify that the reversal was completed.

---

## **Security Alerts and White-Label Agencies**

White-label security notifications protect the agency’s branded experience while still delivering important account-security information. Users receive the security alert through the agency’s branding and domain rather than seeing unrelated platform branding.

Phone-number change alerts are white-label safe and use:

- The agency logo
- The agency domain
- Agency-facing branding

The alerts do not display HighLevel or LeadConnector references when delivered through a white-label agency experience.

This allows agencies to maintain a consistent customer experience while still providing security-sensitive notifications.

---

## **Phone Number Changes and Two-Factor Authentication**

Phone-number change notifications complement existing account-verification safeguards by adding visibility after a security-sensitive update occurs. Users should treat an unexpected phone-number alert seriously because phone numbers may be involved in receiving authentication codes.

HighLevel supports phone-based security codes as part of account access and authentication workflows. Existing troubleshooting guidance also instructs administrators to add a user phone number when SMS security codes are required for login.

The phone-number security alert and reversal process is designed to provide an additional safeguard after a phone-number update. It does not replace other identity-verification or two-factor authentication protections used during account-management workflows.

If a phone-number change was expected, the notification can be treated as confirmation of the update. If it was unexpected, the user can use the reversal link while it remains valid.

---

## **Auditability of Phone Number Reversals**

Recording security-sensitive account activity helps agencies investigate unexpected changes and maintain accountability. HighLevel records phone-number reversals so the action can be traced as part of the account’s security history.

HighLevel Audit Logs provide time-stamped records of supported account activity and can include information about the user, module, action, and affected changes. Audit Logs are available in both agency and sub-account contexts, with the available scope depending on where the activity occurred.

Every phone-number reversal performed through the security recovery process is recorded. For general account-change investigations, authorized users can access Audit Logs from:

- **Agency:** Settings > Audit Logs
- **Sub-Account:** Settings > Audit Logs

Audit Logs can also be filtered by criteria such as user, module, action type, and time range where those filters are available.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081733561/original/AD6uz-ngAGV1tI7aXTeJIB6dcfdr-KdL8Q.png?1790241232)

---

## **How To Use Phone Number Change Security Alerts and Reversal**

Knowing how to respond to a security alert helps users distinguish legitimate account maintenance from an unexpected change. Reviewing the alert promptly is especially important because reversal links are valid for a limited period.

### If you made or expected the change

1. Open the phone-number security notification.
2. Review the change details.
3. Confirm that the time and change origin match the action you expected.
4. No further action is required.

### If you did not expect the change

1. Open the security alert as soon as possible.
2. Confirm that the phone-number change was not authorized by you.
3. Review whether the alert identifies the change as made **by you** or **by your admin**.
4. Click the single-use reversal link.
5. Complete the reversal within **7 days** of the original change.
6. Confirm that the previous phone number has been restored on the confirmation page.
7. Review other account-security settings and contact your agency administrator if you need help investigating the unexpected change.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do I need to take action when I receive a phone-number security alert?**

No. If you recognize and expected the phone-number update, no action is required. The notification serves as confirmation that the change occurred.

**Q: How long is the reversal link valid?**

The single-use reversal link is valid for 7 days.

**Q: Do I need to log in to HighLevel to reverse the change?**

No. The reversal link can restore the previous phone number without requiring a login.

**Q: Can the same reversal link be used multiple times?**

No. The reversal link is single-use.

**Q: Why is an SMS sent to my old phone number?**

When an existing phone number is changed, sending an alert to the previous number helps notify the person who is losing access to that security channel.

**Q: Can I tell whether I changed the phone number or an administrator changed it?**

Yes. The security alert identifies the initiator as either **by you** or **by your admin**.

**Q: Will these notifications display HighLevel branding for a white-label agency?**

No. The alerts are designed to use the agency’s branding and domain for the white-label experience.

**Q: What should I do if my reversal link has expired?**

The self-service reversal link is valid for 7 days. If the link is no longer valid and the phone number needs to be corrected, contact an authorized agency administrator or the appropriate support channel for assistance.

**Q: Are phone-number reversals recorded?**

Yes. Reversal activity is recorded for auditability.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [User Access in HighLevel | Agency & Sub-Accounts](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982600)
- [Audit Logs in HighLevel | Track Changes & User Activity](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006667-audit-logs)
